title: 7G--Special Notice of Intent to Sole Source Award
description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Award THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Communications Branch intends to award a firm fixed price sole source under the authority of FAR subpart 13.106-1(b)(1)(i) and (ii), for purchases not exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT), Contracting Officers may solicit from only one source if the circumstances deem only one source is reasonably available (e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand name, or industrial mobilization).: Biomark, LLC. 705 S 8TH ST Boise, Idaho 83702-7112, United States The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334511, Other Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical, and Nautical System and Instrument Manufacturing. Service Code (PSC) for this requirement is 7G22, IT and Telecom, Network: Satellite and Rf Communications Products. The object of this sole source award is to acquire the purchase of 40,000 PIT tags with 1334 KBRA funding earmarked for monitoring equipment and expiring 256 1311 funding from Biomark, along with 8 new submersible antenna batteries. The PIT tags proposed are the APT12 preloaded needles, 12mm full duplex tags, sold in flats of 100 tags per tray. These tags are generally used to mark all wild reared Lost River and Shortnose Suckers reared on station and then repatriated to Upper Klamath Lake and its tributaries for population monitoring purposes. We are currently low on tags and need to acquire tags for this coming fall work to tag our 2026 cohort of production fish. In addition, we need some new submersible antenna batteries to replace older ones that don't function anymore, as these will be used to monitor these endangered suckers in the wild, post stocking, at additional designated sites in Upper Klamath Lake. As for PIT tag submersible antenna replacement batteries, these are unique to BioMark equipment we already have or for the application whereby we'll be using these, allowing us to detect both full duplex and half duplex PIT tags. While others manufacture a similar tag that is utilized for similar purposes, there are significant concerns regarding the consistency and reliability of their tags. Specifically, there is no guarantee that those other tags will yield the same level of detections. There has been minimal use of these vendor's tags by Federal, State, and Tribal agencies to date as compared to Biomark. This variability poses a risk to fisheries management, as inconsistent detection rates and other potential variable can lead to unreliable data and potentially hinder effective decision-making. This synopsis does not constitute a solicitation; however, if any interested party believes they can meet the above requirement, it may submit a statement of capabilities. The statement of capabilities must be submitted in writing and must contain clear and convincing evidence that competition of this requirement would be advantageous to the Government. If parties choose to respond, any cost associated with preparation and submission of data or any other cost incurred in response to this announcement are the sole responsibility of the respondent and will not be reimbursed by the Government. Capability statements shall be submitted by e-mail ONLY as a Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF attachment to the following address: carter_duke@ios.doi.gov. NO TELEPHONE REQUESTS/OFFERS WILL BE HONORED

title: Submarine Force Museum Museum Display Cases
description: The purpose of amendment 0001 on 9/3 is to add the PDF copy of the SOW that includes the photos. The purpose of amendment 0002 is to extend the close date to 9/15. The Submarine Force Museum (SFM) intends to procure two (2) conservation-grade (i.e. made from archival materials that are inert and will not off-gas or cause damage to the artifacts) microclimate museum display cases for use in future exhibits. This is part of a broader strategy to update all cases in the museum to have a uniform appearance and to meet museum preservation standards. These cases will help SFM meet current preservation standards while displaying artifacts from its historic collections, as the current cases which can accommodate mannequins do not meet museum preservation standards and are causing degradation to the artifacts on display. These cases will increase flexibility and mobility when creating new exhibits, as they are moveable, unlike the current cases. Conservation-grade cases will also allow SFM to borrow artifacts from other institutions which require more stringent display preservation standards than the current cases allow. These new cases will replace a double mannequin case that was previously loaned to SFM but is now being recalled. These cases will allow SFM to continue displaying the two mannequins assigned to this exhibit, thus preventing disruption of display and the visitor experience. These new cases should align with the design, engineering, and appearance of the ones already installed in the exhibit (see reference photos below; these cases were the first to be designed and engineered as part of the case updating strategy and therefore, they form the benchmark by which all other cases will be created), with any desired differences and exceptions noted here. Please see attached solicitation for full details.

description: This is a notice of intent to award a sole source contract and is not a request for quotes. The Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA) Network Contracting Office NCO2, on behalf of VISN2 South Medical Centers, intends to award a Firm Fixed Price (FFP), sole source action to: Name of Contractor: QIAGEN LLC Street Address: 19300 Germantown Road City, State, Zip: Germantown, MD 20874-1415 VISN02 medical centers have a recurring requirement for US Food & Drug Administration (FDA) approved In Vitro Diagnostic (IVD), cell mediated immunity (IGRA) tests for detecting Mycobacterium infections using chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA) on LIAISON analyzers. Market research was conducted in accordance with FAR Part 10, reviewing the offerings and capabilities available through the current marketplace. In accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 6.103-1, it has been determined that only one source is reasonably available, QIAGEN LLC. QIAGEN is the manufacturer and sole distributor of the QuantiFERON TB Gold testing. QuantiFERON is the only test capable of meeting the salient characteristics of the requirement and providing the necessary compatibility with the Department of Veterans Affairs existing LIAISON analyzers. Market research failed to produce additional sources capable of fulfilling this requirement as a whole; No subcontracting opportunities are available for this requirement. In accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) this notice of intent to sole source with justification to limit sources, satisfies the public posting requirements. Veterans Health Administration prohibits the use of gray market items in their Medical Centers. Gray market items are considered to be items outside of the original equipment manufacturer s intended distribution channels. This notice is not a request for quotes; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement which shall be considered by the Government. All capability statements must be received by no later than 10:00 AM Eastern Standard Time on September 15, 2025. Responses to be submitted to Lindsay Goldsmith, Contracting Officer at lindsay.goldsmith@va.gov. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: MRTC Parking Lot Refresh
description: Marine Forces Special Operations Command, (MARSOC), Marine Raider Center (MRC), Camp Lejeune, NC has a requirement to repair/fill cracks and seal approximately 130,000 square feet of parking lot at RR450 parking lots. The general scope of work includes cleaning, filling, smoothing, and sealing both parking lots around RR450. The following Objectives are provided: 1. Mandatory Site Visit and Base Access Requirements A mandatory site visit will be conducted on 27 August at 0900 EST at the Building RR450 parking lot, Stone Bay, MCB Camp Lejeune, NC. Mandatory Attendance: Attendance at this site visit is mandatory. Only those vendors who attend the site visit in its entirety will be eligible to submit quotes in response to this solicitation. Quotes received from vendors who did not attend the site visit will be rejected without evaluation. Base Access Request Deadline: To gain access to the MARFORSOC compound at Stone Bay, contractor personnel must be vetted. Vendors must submit their base access request documentation to the Contracting Officer (Samuel Williams) and the Contract Specialist via email no later than 24 August. Access Request Content: The access request must be submitted on the visiting company's official stationery, signed by a company authority, and contain the following information for each attendee (limit of 2 attendees per company): Full Legal Name (Last, First, Middle) Date of Birth Place of Birth Citizenship Driver's License Number and State of Issuance 2. Questions Offerors shall submit all questions regarding this solicitation via email to the POCs listed below no later than 10:00AM EST on September 9, 2026. The Government will consolidate all questions and issue an official amendment on SAM.gov. Contracting Officer: Krissia Avelares Valle (krissia.i.avelaresvalle.mil@socom.mil) Contracting Specialist: Spenser Gagnon (spenser.e.gagnon.civ@socom.mil) 3. Proposal Submission Instructions Eligible offerors (who attended the mandatory site visit) shall submit their proposals via email to the Contracting Office. Proposals must be submitted in three (3) separate and distinct volumes as outlined below. Page limits must be strictly adhered to; any pages exceeding the limit will not be evaluated. All proposals are due Volume Title Page Limit Submission Requirements Volume I Technical Capability 6 Pages Max Technical Approach, Equipment List, Personnel Overview, and Draft Construction Phasing Plan. Volume II Past Performance 2 Pages Max Up to three (3) Past Performance References of similar scope and complexity. Volume III Price No Limit Completed SF 1449 Schedule of Supplies/Services, Price Breakdown, and Representations & Certifications. 4. Volume Content Requirements A. Volume I: Technical Capability The Technical Volume must clearly demonstrate the offeror's capability to perform the requirements set forth in the Statement of Work (SOW). Boilerplate or repeating the SOW language without detail is unacceptable. The volume must include: Technical Approach: A detailed narrative describing how the offeror will execute SOW Objectives #1 through #6, specifically outlining the crack cleaning process, crack-filling application (Objective #2), seal coat application and mixing ratio (Objective #3), restriping and stenciling (Objective #4), parking block replacement and installation (Objective #5), and the handicap sign post installations (Objective #6). Draft Construction Phasing Plan: A draft plan showing how the offeror will execute the work while maintaining at least fifty percent (50%) parking capacity operational continuity at Building RR450 at all times. The plan must include a tentative Gantt chart schedule within the 120-day Period of Performance and explain how emergency vehicle access will be guaranteed. Security and Base Access Compliance: A brief statement acknowledging and demonstrating a plan to comply with Camp Lejeune base access regulations (NCIC checks) and coordinating with MARSOC-provided escorts. B. Volume II: Past Performance Offerors shall submit up to three (3) past performance references for federal, state, local, or commercial contracts executed within the past three (3) years that are similar in scope and complexity to the RR450 requirement (e.g., parking lot sealing, crack filling, and striping requirements exceeding 50,000 sq ft). Each reference must include: Contract Number, Customer Name, and Point of Contact (Email and Phone). Period of Performance and Total Contract Dollar Value. A brief description of the work performed, highlighting similarities to the RR450 scope of work, specifically mentioning the total square footage treated and whether phasing or escort requirements were managed. Note: Offerors may submit standard reference letters in lieu of, or in addition to, the contact list. C. Volume III: Price The offeror shall submit a fully completed SF 1449 schedule with firm-fixed-prices (FFP) for the single, lump-sum CLIN (0001). The offeror must also submit a supporting price breakdown detailing direct material costs, direct labor costs (complying with Davis-Bacon Wage Determination No. NC20260090), mobilization, project management/overhead, and bond costs.

title: 66--Special Notice of Intent to Sole Source Award
description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Award THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Communications Branch intends to award a firm fixed price sole source under the authority of FAR subpart 13.106-1(b)(1)(i) and (ii), for purchases not exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT), Contracting Officers may solicit from only one source if the circumstances deem only one source is reasonably available (e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand name, or industrial mobilization).: Biomark, LLC. 705 S 8TH ST Boise, Idaho 83702-7112, United States The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334511, Other Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical, and Nautical System and Instrument Manufacturing. Service Code (PSC) for this requirement is 7G22, IT and Telecom, Network: Satellite and Rf Communications Products. The object of this sole source award is to acquire the purchase of VAKI Micro Splithead digital camera/counter head and VAKI specified PC. Confirmed through VAKI that replacement components must be OEM due to proprietary firmware and software. No alternate manufacturers produce compatible camera heads or system PCs. General market review found no equivalent products that integrate with existing VAKI systems. No other vendors produce components compatible with VAKIs proprietary hardware, firmware, or software. NonOEM parts cannot interface with the system and would void support. No other sources expressed capability. Proprietary optical components; firmware locked to OEM hardware; system requires OEMcertified installation, configuration, and support. These factors prevent competition for the required replacement equipment. VAKI is the original equipment manufacturer for the Micro Splithead system and the sole provider of compatible hardware, firmware, and service. Only VAKI can supply components that maintain system functionality and support. This synopsis does not constitute a solicitation; however, if any interested party believes they can meet the above requirement, it may submit a statement of capabilities. The statement of capabilities must be submitted in writing and must contain clear and convincing evidence that competition of this requirement would be advantageous to the Government. If parties choose to respond, any cost associated with preparation and submission of data or any other cost incurred in response to this announcement are the sole responsibility of the respondent and will not be reimbursed by the Government. Capability statements shall be submitted by e-mail ONLY as a Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF attachment to the following address: carter_duke@ios.doi.gov. NO TELEPHONE REQUESTS/OFFERS WILL BE HONORED

NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Award THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. Service Code (PSC) for this requirement is 7G22, IT and Telecom, Network: Satellite and Rf Communications Products. The object of this sole source award is to acquire the purchase of INNOVASEA (formerly Vemco) brand acoustic telemetry work in our field work operations. INNOVASEA is the only company that supplies acoustic receivers/tags to all other agencies/projects participating in the Great Lakes Acoustic Telemetry Observation System (GLATOS) funded by the Great Lakes Fishery Commission. Other company's products are not compatible with the INNOVASEA system, and would therefore not be a part of the Great Lakes wide GLATOS data network for reporting tag detections. Since this project and our current/former projects will be a part of the GLATOS network and will utilize existing INNOVASEA equipment already deployed, it is not possible to use other company's equipment. This synopsis does not constitute a solicitation; however, if any interested party believes they can meet the above requirement, it may submit a statement of capabilities. title: Dataminr, Inc. First Alert Advanced
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE The Defense Information Systems Agency/Defense Information Technology Contracting Organization (DISA/DITCO) intends to negotiate a sole source contract with Dataminr, Inc. A sole source Justification & Approval document is currently being coordinated and, upon approval, a copy of it will be posted here on SAM.gov to comply with the public display requirements of FAR 6.301. The proposed contract action is to procure annual software licenses and support for Dataminr�s First Alert Advanced (P/N: DM-FAFC-ADV-IND), a proprietary, commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) real-time, AI-powered intelligence platform. This new Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) contract will upgrade the Government's existing First Alert licensing posture into a single, unified vehicle, while expanding capacity to support new requirements for additional Government partners. The contract structure includes a 12-month Base Year and four (4) 12-month Option Years. The Government is seeking 50 base First Alert Advanced individual use licenses with up to 21 optional licenses to support joint Government operations. The First Alert Advanced platform represents a critical technological evolution that introduces proprietary Agentic AI capabilities essential to the Government's mission. These capabilities include Tactical Predictive Intelligence, which leverages Dataminr�s proprietary 13+ year historical data archive to predict how an event may evolve. It also includes Agentic Corroboration & Context, which deploys a fleet of AI agents to instantly scan over 200,000 distinct public information sources�including social media, IoT sensor data, audio transmissions, and the dark web�providing real-time verification. Furthermore, the Government requires the unique capability to track and analyze anomalous airplane transponder signals (ADS-B Signals). The Dataminr First Alert Advanced platform consumes tens of millions of data points per day from radar, ground, and space-based ADS-B receiving stations worldwide. The platform uses proprietary AI methods�ranging from statistical event modeling to deep learning and machine learning�to detect anomalies in this time-series data, alerting watch-standers to critical national security events such as aircraft diverting from scheduled routes or exhibiting unexpected shifts in altitude or course. At this time, the incumbent contractor and original equipment manufacturer (OEM), Dataminr, Inc., is the only source capable of providing all necessary services. The requirement constitutes a highly specialized upgrade of existing, integrated Government software that relies entirely on proprietary data feeds, closed-source algorithms, and intellectual property owned exclusively by the OEM. Dataminr, Inc. maintains no authorized resellers or distributors. No other commercial vendor has the legal right or technical capability to access the existing Government infrastructure, modify the current software instances, or integrate the proprietary "Advanced" agentic AI modules. The statutory authority for other than full and open competition is 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Companies who believe they can provide this service must indicate their interest in writing within 15 calendar days of this notification and include a detailed capability statement. No reimbursement for any cost connected with providing capability information will be provided. All responsible sources will be considered in evaluating the determination to issue a sole-source contract. Quotations or proposals received in response to this notice cannot be accepted since this synopsis cannot be considered a request for quote or a request for proposal. A solicitation will NOT be posted to SAM.gov due to the sole source nature of the requirement. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 518210 (Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services) will be used for determining company size status. CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND: This requirement is an ongoing capability requirement that is expanding in capacity. Portions of this requirement are currently being executed under the following legacy contracts, which will not have their remaining options exercised in order to facilitate this unified upgrade to the Advanced platform: Contract Number: HC1047-24-C-0010 Contract Type: Firm Fixed Price Incumbent and their size and CAGE: Dataminr, Inc., Large Business, CAGE Code 6Q6Z6 Method of previous acquisition: Sole Source Period of performance: 22 September 2024 � 21 September 2030 Contract Number: HC1047-23-C-0009 Contract Type: Firm Fixed Price Incumbent and their size and CAGE: Dataminr, Inc., Large Business, CAGE Code 6Q6Z6 Method of previous acquisition: Sole Source Period of performance: 22 September 2023 � 21 September 2027 Point of Contact: karoline.k.schmal.civ@mail.mil

title: MRTC Parking Lot Refresh
description: **Amendment to add Q&A and Parking Lot Diagram** Marine Forces Special Operations Command, (MARSOC), Marine Raider Center (MRC), Camp Lejeune, NC has a requirement to repair/fill cracks and seal approximately 130,000 square feet of parking lot at RR450 parking lots. The general scope of work includes cleaning, filling, smoothing, and sealing both parking lots around RR450. The following Objectives are provided: 1. Mandatory Site Visit and Base Access Requirements A mandatory site visit will be conducted on 27 August at 0900 EST at the Building RR450 parking lot, Stone Bay, MCB Camp Lejeune, NC. Mandatory Attendance: Attendance at this site visit is mandatory. Only those vendors who attend the site visit in its entirety will be eligible to submit quotes in response to this solicitation. Quotes received from vendors who did not attend the site visit will be rejected without evaluation. Base Access Request Deadline: To gain access to the MARFORSOC compound at Stone Bay, contractor personnel must be vetted. Vendors must submit their base access request documentation to the Contracting Officer (Samuel Williams) and the Contract Specialist via email no later than 24 August. Access Request Content: The access request must be submitted on the visiting company's official stationery, signed by a company authority, and contain the following information for each attendee (limit of 2 attendees per company): Full Legal Name (Last, First, Middle) Date of Birth Place of Birth Citizenship Driver's License Number and State of Issuance 2. Questions Offerors shall submit all questions regarding this solicitation via email to the POCs listed below no later than 10:00AM EST on September 9, 2026. The Government will consolidate all questions and issue an official amendment on SAM.gov. Contracting Officer: Krissia Avelares Valle (krissia.i.avelaresvalle.mil@socom.mil) Contracting Specialist: Spenser Gagnon (spenser.e.gagnon.civ@socom.mil) 3. Proposal Submission Instructions Eligible offerors (who attended the mandatory site visit) shall submit their proposals via email to the Contracting Office. Proposals must be submitted in three (3) separate and distinct volumes as outlined below. Page limits must be strictly adhered to; any pages exceeding the limit will not be evaluated. All proposals are due Volume Title Page Limit Submission Requirements Volume I Technical Capability 6 Pages Max Technical Approach, Equipment List, Personnel Overview, and Draft Construction Phasing Plan. Volume II Past Performance 2 Pages Max Up to three (3) Past Performance References of similar scope and complexity. Volume III Price No Limit Completed SF 1449 Schedule of Supplies/Services, Price Breakdown, and Representations & Certifications. 4. Volume Content Requirements A. Volume I: Technical Capability The Technical Volume must clearly demonstrate the offeror's capability to perform the requirements set forth in the Statement of Work (SOW). Boilerplate or repeating the SOW language without detail is unacceptable. The volume must include: Technical Approach: A detailed narrative describing how the offeror will execute SOW Objectives #1 through #6, specifically outlining the crack cleaning process, crack-filling application (Objective #2), seal coat application and mixing ratio (Objective #3), restriping and stenciling (Objective #4), parking block replacement and installation (Objective #5), and the handicap sign post installations (Objective #6). Draft Construction Phasing Plan: A draft plan showing how the offeror will execute the work while maintaining at least fifty percent (50%) parking capacity operational continuity at Building RR450 at all times. The plan must include a tentative Gantt chart schedule within the 120-day Period of Performance and explain how emergency vehicle access will be guaranteed. Security and Base Access Compliance: A brief statement acknowledging and demonstrating a plan to comply with Camp Lejeune base access regulations (NCIC checks) and coordinating with MARSOC-provided escorts. B. Volume II: Past Performance Offerors shall submit up to three (3) past performance references for federal, state, local, or commercial contracts executed within the past three (3) years that are similar in scope and complexity to the RR450 requirement (e.g., parking lot sealing, crack filling, and striping requirements exceeding 50,000 sq ft). Each reference must include: Contract Number, Customer Name, and Point of Contact (Email and Phone). Period of Performance and Total Contract Dollar Value. A brief description of the work performed, highlighting similarities to the RR450 scope of work, specifically mentioning the total square footage treated and whether phasing or escort requirements were managed. Note: Offerors may submit standard reference letters in lieu of, or in addition to, the contact list. C. Volume III: Price The offeror shall submit a fully completed SF 1449 schedule with firm-fixed-prices (FFP) for the single, lump-sum CLIN (0001). The offeror must also submit a supporting price breakdown detailing direct material costs, direct labor costs (complying with Davis-Bacon Wage Determination No. NC20260090), mobilization, project management/overhead, and bond costs.

title: Coastal Storm Risk Management (CSRM) At Surf City, North Carolina - Industry Day
description: Special Notice: W912PM27BA001 Title: Industry Day for FY26/FY 27 Coastal Storm Risk Management Surf City, North Carolina The Industry Day Meeting for the Coastal Storm Risk Management (CSRM) Surf City will occur on 15 September 2026 at 11:00 AM EST via Teams. The work consists of furnishing plant, labor, materials, and equipment to perform dredging, transporting, placing and shaping beach fill and performing all pre and post construction beach surveys. Approximately 1 borrow areas is available for the project and located offshore of Topsail Island Beaches at the south end of the island. The Surf City Coastal Storm Risk Management Project consists of placing 6,500,000 CY of Dune and Berm beach fill along approximately 33,300 LF of Surf City Beach. This project shall use either an ocean certified hopper and/or an ocean certified pipeline dredge. The project also consists of extending approximately 40 existing walkover structures in Surf City and the stabilization of approximately 46 to 56 acres of new dune. In addition, breakout sessions will be provided with individual contractors following the group industry day meeting. Please indicate with your RSVP if you would like to request a breakout meeting. Please RSVP no later than 3PM ET 11 September 2026 to both Ros Shoemaker and Jenifer Garland at Rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil and jenifer.m.garland@usace.army.mil if you plan to attend the Industry Day and/or request a breakout session. A Teams calendar invite will be sent out to all RSVP�s.

title: Coastal Storm Risk Management (CSRM) At Surf City, North Carolina - Industry Day
description: Special Notice: W912PM27BA001 Title: Industry Day for FY26/FY 27 Coastal Storm Risk Management Surf City, North Carolina The Industry Day Meeting for the Coastal Storm Risk Management (CSRM) Surf City will occur on 15 September 2026 at 11:00 AM EST via Teams. The work consists of furnishing plant, labor, materials, and equipment to perform dredging, transporting, placing and shaping beach fill and performing all pre and post construction beach surveys. Approximately 1 borrow areas is available for the project and located offshore of Topsail Island Beaches at the south end of the island. The Surf City Coastal Storm Risk Management Project consists of placing 6,500,000 CY of Dune and Berm beach fill along approximately 33,300 LF of Surf City Beach. This project shall use either an ocean certified hopper and/or an ocean certified pipeline dredge. The project also consists of extending approximately 40 existing walkover structures in Surf City and the stabilization of approximately 46 to 56 acres of new dune. In addition, breakout sessions will be provided with individual contractors following the group industry day meeting. Please indicate with your RSVP if you would like to request a breakout meeting. Please RSVP no later than 3PM ET 11 September 2026 to both Ros Shoemaker and Jenifer Garland at Rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil and jenifer.m.garland@usace.army.mil if you plan to attend the Industry Day and/or request a breakout session. title: Psychological Health and Safety Data Analysis
description: In compliance with FAR Subpart 12.202 (a) coupled with the provisions set forth by FAR Subpart 5.101(a)(1), this Notice is hereby published to inform of the following: The Chicago District intends to award a sole source contract to TOR INTELLIGENCE, LLC (UEI: FBC2UMLZKHE4). This requirement is for the following: The USACE Chicago District requires expert-level human factors analysis, safety analytics, psychological health program evaluation, and workforce data correlation services. The contractor shall: a. Analyze a minimum of five (5) years of USACE safety, accident, and human factors program data. b. Review and evaluate existing data sets and reporting systems, including the Federal Employee Viewpoint Survey (FEVS), Critical Command Incident Reports (CCIRs), Safety Incident Boards (SIBs), Worker Compensation financial claims data, and related enterprise systems. c. Perform a comprehensive audit of USACE psychological health programs (resilience initiatives, employee assistance programs, and behavioral health resources). d. Conduct cross-system correlation analysis between mandatory/optional training completion rates and incident occurrences. e. Deliver actionable recommendations, executive summaries, white papers, and leadership presentations aimed at mitigating workforce risk factors, enhancing organizational resilience, and reducing worker compensation costs. The Government intends to obtain a quote solely from TOR INTELLIGENCE, LLC under the authority of RFO 12.102(a) due to only one source being reasonably available to meet the needs of the Government. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code will be 541690, the size standard will be $19,000,000.00 and the Product Service Code (PSC) will be R410. Please be advised the aforementioned information is anticipatory in nature and is not binding. This notice is not a request for competitive quotes; however, any responsible source believing that it can fulfill the requirement may be considered by the agency. Interested parties may identify their interest and capabilities in response to this synopsis and must clearly show the ability of the firm to be responsive without compromising the quality, accuracy, and reliability of services provided. title: S2 Cognition
description: Title: S2 Cognition Description: The 5th Special Forces Group (Airborne) at Fort Campbell, KY, requires a one-year license agreement for a comprehensive Cognitive Performance Assessment System. This system is essential for evaluating and enhancing the cognitive abilities of Special Forces operators, which are critical for mission success in high-stress, dynamic environments. The required solution includes the provision of a scientifically validated cognitive testing platform, all necessary hardware, software licenses, and related support services. The primary objective is to measure and analyze the cognitive processes that underlie rapid, split-second decision-making. Questions are due August 31, 2026 1400 CST. Responses are due September 15, 2026 1000 CST. Key Requirements: Cognitive Assessment: The system must be a computer-based testing platform capable of measuring cognitive performance with millisecond precision. It must assess at least thirteen specific cognitive domains, including but not limited to perception speed, search efficiency, decision complexity, and impulse control. Hardware and Software: The contractor shall provide all necessary equipment, including testing consoles, monitors, and peripherals, along with the required software licenses, maintenance, and updates. Data and Analysis: The solution must include secure database storage for all assessment results and provide consultation services for score interpretation relative to Special Operations roles. Validation: The testing protocols and equipment must be scientifically based, using statistically validated methods, and demonstrate test-retest reliability. This is a brand-name requirement for the "S2 Cognition" system. Offerors must propose the specified brand-name product to be considered technically acceptable. Quotes for alternate or "equal" products will not be accepted. For a complete list of requirements and salient characteristics, please refer to the attached solicitation documents.
